correctness.rationale: Direct incidence matrix-unit multiplication yields five explicit commutator rows. Partition by endpoint diagonal equality; with distinct endpoints the long interval gives a private pivot and two independent chain factors. With equal endpoints classify zero, one or two active chains; private pivots, the four-cycle graphic rank and a one-equation affine scalar condition determine every rank multiplicity. The cases are exhaustive in every characteristic. Exact q2 and q3 brute-force Gaussian elimination agrees for all ranks, and R_q(1)=q^9 is symbolic, not a proof substitute.

value.rationale: The diamond is the minimal poset with two distinct length-two paths and nonzero products of radical elements. It is thus the first non-square-zero obstruction to all-field incidence-algebra rank spectra governed by weighted graphic-matroid methods. The complete six-stratum all-q count is an exact canonical boundary benchmark, includes rank five unavailable in the 4-edge radical-square-zero model, and supplies exact centralizer/commuting data for testing future height-three formulas. It is not an arbitrary numerical parameter slice or a claimed general theorem.
